parts.text: Define electric potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
An isolated conducting sphere is charged. Fig. 5.1 shows the variation of the potential *V* due to the sphere with displacement *x* from its centre.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
Two spheres are identical to the sphere in (b). Each sphere has the same charge as the sphere in (b).

The spheres are held in a vacuum so that their centres are separated by a distance of 0.46 m. Assume that the charge on each sphere is a point charge at the centre of the sphere.
parts.text: Calculate the electric potential energy *E*ₚ of the two spheres.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The two spheres are now released simultaneously so that they are free to move.

Describe and explain the subsequent motion of the spheres.

figures.alt: A graph of potential V against displacement x, with a symmetric curve that falls to a flat minimum around the centre and rises towards both outer edges.
